text:
Ravi Nair: Heads-up — p95 for /v1/chat (prod-us) jumped ~60ms after the kernel swap at 03:12. Flame graphs in the profiler: https://perf.redwood/reports/1766667890

Maya Chen: Saw that. KV hit-rate drop too? Any traces showing prefix churn?

Eli Gomez: Yep. KV hit-rate 91% -> 68% on chat routes. Traces show more frequent short-prefix evictions. Looks correlated with the attn_opt_v2 kernel landing.

Sofia Park: Quick sample from the profiler attached:
```
# top samples
kernel:attn_opt_v2  48%
kernel:matmul_v1    27%
kv_lookup          15%
other              10%
```

Ravi Nair: Hmm. attn_opt_v2 seems to reduce throughput for very small minibatches due to per-invocation prefetch + kernel startup. That would push more microbatches and bust KV locality.

Anya (oncall): Note: we also rolled the token-budget-by-tier tweak last night (free tier token_target 256 -> 192). Could amplify small-batch pattern.

Maya Chen: That matches. Lower token_target -> more microbatches -> less stable KV heat. Proposal: revert free-tier token_target to 256 as a canary, keep kernel, observe p95 for 30m.

Eli Gomez: Alternative is to keep token_target but change queue policy for chat routes to hold a bit longer (trade a few ms queue wait for much lower p95).

PerfBot: deploy started: canary/restore-freebudget @ 1766667950 by Maya Chen

Sofia Park: Config A (restore budget) vs Config B (kernel with queue-hold) snippets for quick A/B:
```
# Config A
route_tiers:
  free:
    token_target: 256
# Config B
queue_policy:
  chat_routes:
    hold_ms: 12
    token_target: 440
  short_queries:
    hold_ms: 4
    token_target: 80
```

Ravi Nair: Also add a small KV prefetch window (+10ms) for the attn_opt_v2 codepath so we warm more prefixes before kernel runs. Low-risk and easy to toggle.

Maya Chen: On it. I'll patch runtime config and wire up the perf dashboard to show p50/p95 and kv_hit_rate side-by-side. Alert at p95 > target for 5m.

Eli Gomez: Added perf markers in the serving runtime so we can correlate kernel entry time vs first kv miss. Helps prove causality.

PerfBot: canary complete: revert applied @ 1766668030 — monitoring window open (90s)

Anya (oncall): Early telemetry: p95 returned to baseline within ~45s. KV hit-rate recovering to ~89%. No increased errors.

Ravi Nair: Nice. Follow-ups: 1) run synthetic sweep (prompt lengths 16/64/256) to stress token targets and measure p95 curve; 2) add microbench unit for kernel launch penalty; 3) for attn_opt_v2 rollout, do a soft-launch that temporarily raises token_target for affected tiers by +30% to preserve batch sizes.

Maya Chen: Making tickets now (ENG-1287 backlog). I'll schedule the synthetic sweep for tomorrow's perf window.

Eli Gomez: Will attach flame graphs per prompt length and the kv eviction histogram to the ticket.

Sofia Park: Also recommend adding a short-lived experiment: increase hold_ms only for routes with high prefix reuse, so we don't penalize short ad-hoc queries.

Ravi Nair: Agreed. Thanks everyone. If p95 creeps again, revert is the plan and we keep the kernel off for full rollout until we have the token-budget/hold heuristics tuned. :thumbsup:
